approvals.searchPlaceholder: Search by token, tool, or reason...
approvals.emptyPending: No pending approvals. Tokens with Confirm-mode capabilities will create requests here.
approvals.reasonPlaceholder: Explain why this request was rejected
approvals.rejectWithErrorTitle: Reject and send the card's configuration error back to the agent as the reason
approvals.diffWholeLayout: Showing the proposed layout (the After side).
approvals.diffCardBefore: Showing the card being removed or replaced.

cap_config_read.label: Configuration read
cap_config_read.description: Read Home Assistant configuration and event listener counts.

cap_template_render.label: Template render
cap_template_render.description: Render Jinja templates using entities this token can access.

cap_log_read.label: System log read
cap_log_read.description: Read Home Assistant system log entries.

cap_search.label: Search & discovery
cap_search.description: Find and describe entities, areas, and relationships within this token's scope.

cap_registry_read.label: Registry read
cap_registry_read.description: List areas, floors, zones, and devices that contain accessible entities.

cap_traces.label: Automation traces
cap_traces.description: Read execution traces to troubleshoot automations.

cap_diagnostics.label: Diagnostics
cap_diagnostics.description: Check system health and validate automation, script, and scene YAML.

cap_broadcast.label: Broadcast
cap_broadcast.description: Make announcements through Assist satellite devices.

cap_service_response.label: Service response data
cap_service_response.description: Return data from services that provide a response, such as conversation.process.

cap_automation_write.label: Manage automations
cap_automation_write.description: Create, edit, and delete automations. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_script_write.label: Manage scripts
cap_script_write.description: Create, edit, and delete scripts. Bypasses entity-level access controls.

cap_blueprint_write.label: Manage blueprints
cap_blueprint_write.description: Create, edit, and delete blueprints. Also requires the matching automation or script capability. Editing a blueprint reloads every automation or script built from it, so one change can rewire several at once.

cap_scene_write.label: Manage scenes
cap_scene_write.description: Create, edit, and delete scenes. Referenced entities are still subject to MESA and entity access.

cap_helper_write.label: Manage helpers
cap_helper_write.description: Create, edit, and delete helpers such as inputs, counters, and timers.

cap_physical_control.label: Physical control
cap_physical_control.description: Control locks, alarms, covers, and valves.

cap_restart.label: Restart or stop Home Assistant
cap_restart.description: Allow homeassistant.restart and homeassistant.stop service calls.

cap_integration_write.label: Integration management
cap_integration_write.description: Enable or disable Home Assistant integrations.

cap_lovelace_write.label: Manage dashboards
cap_lovelace_write.description: Create, edit, and delete Lovelace dashboards.

cap_registry_write.label: Manage entity registry
cap_registry_write.description: Edit entity names, icons, and areas, or delete stale entries. Entity IDs cannot be renamed.

cap_radio_write.label: Radio management
cap_radio_write.description: Pair, re-interview, and remove Zigbee devices through Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA.

cap_backup.label: Backup
cap_backup.description: Create and list backups. Restore them from Home Assistant.

cap_filesystem.label: Filesystem access
cap_filesystem.description: Read and write files under www/, themes/, and custom_templates/.

cap_esphome_yaml.label: ESPHome device YAML
cap_esphome_yaml.description: Read and edit ESPHome device YAML in its own jail under esphome/, validate it, and compile it. Credentials are masked on read and cannot be changed. Compiling only builds a binary; flashing a device needs the separate ESPHome firmware flashing capability.

cap_esphome_flash.label: ESPHome firmware flashing
cap_esphome_flash.description: Install compiled firmware onto an ESPHome device over the air, replacing what it is running. A bad image can leave a device unreachable until it is reflashed over a cable, so Confirm is strongly recommended.

cap_yaml_edit.label: Edit raw YAML
cap_yaml_edit.description: Read and edit configuration.yaml directly. Approval is strongly recommended. Inline secrets are exposed, so store secrets in secrets.yaml with !secret.

caps.modeDescConfirm: Queue each call for approval in this panel.
caps.passThroughNotice: Pass-through is enabled. Reads and everyday actions are treated as Allow. Configuration changes, system actions, high-risk capabilities, and system log access still use the settings below. Confirm always requires approval.
caps.esphomeBadgeTitle: The ESPHome tools stay hidden from this token until the add-on is available. The capability can still be set now.

automation_builder.label: Automation builder
automation_builder.description: Can discover entities and manage automations, scripts, scenes, and helpers. Restarts and physical controls require approval.

dashboard_designer.label: Dashboard designer
dashboard_designer.description: Can discover entities and build dashboards. Theme and custom card files require approval. Cannot control devices or edit other configuration.

esphome.label: ESPHome devices
esphome.description: Reads ESPHome device status, diagnostics, and logs. Editing device YAML and flashing firmware each need approval. YAML credentials stay hidden and unchangeable. No device control or other configuration.

personas.helper: A persona sets the initial capabilities. You can adjust individual capabilities in Advanced. The persona changes to Custom when your settings no longer match a preset.

home_admin.label: Home administrator
home_admin.description: Can read and manage the whole home. Restarts, physical controls, and sensitive configuration changes require approval.

maintenance.label: Maintenance / backups
maintenance.description: Can run diagnostics and create backups. Restarts and entity registry changes require approval. Cannot control devices or edit configuration and dashboards.

new_user.label: New user
new_user.description: Can read your home and control only the devices you grant. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval. You can change this later.

personas.noEsphome: ESPHome was not detected on this system

power_user.label: Power user
power_user.description: Can read and edit most configuration and restart Home Assistant. Sensitive system changes require approval. Filesystem and raw YAML access stay blocked.

read_only.label: Read-only observer
read_only.description: Can read states, history, logs, and templates. Cannot run actions or announcements.

voice_assistant.label: Voice assistant
voice_assistant.description: Can read entities, run services, and make announcements. Locks, alarms, covers, and valves require approval.

tokens.heroSub: Give an AI agent scoped, revocable access to Home Assistant. The setup wizard creates a token and helps you connect the agent.
tokens.maxWarning: You have reached the recommended maximum of {max} active tokens. Consider revoking unused tokens.
tokens.filterAria: Filter tokens by name or status
tokens.empty: No tokens yet. Create one to get started.
tokens.announceAllHelp: Show every Phoenix MCP tool, including tools this token cannot use. Leave off to reduce model usage and avoid failed calls. Enable for troubleshooting only.
tokens.assistExposureHelp: For pass-through tokens, show only entities exposed to Home Assistant Assist. Scoped tokens use the permission tree instead.
tokens.clearPermsBody: This removes every domain, device, and entity grant. The token will have no entity access until you add new permissions.
tokens.createPtUnderstand: I understand this token has broad Home Assistant access
tokens.createPtWarning: This token gets broad access to Home Assistant entities and services. Configuration changes, system actions, high-risk capabilities, and system log access still use the Capabilities settings. MESA rules, the Phoenix MCP blocklist, sensitive attribute removal, rate limits, revocation, and expiry also remain active. Use it only with trusted HTTP-based MCP clients.
tokens.emulatorPassThrough: Pass Through tokens bypass the permission tree, so every non-Phoenix entity resolves to write. No simulation needed.
tokens.enablePtBody: Pass-through gives this token broad entity and service access. Configuration changes, system actions, high-risk capabilities, system log access, MESA rules, the Phoenix MCP blocklist, and sensitive attribute removal still apply.
tokens.enablePtCheck: I understand this token will have broad Home Assistant access
tokens.helpConnect: Help me connect this token to an agent
tokens.inlineWaitDisabled: Currently disabled. Choose a duration to enable it.
tokens.inlineWaitHelp: How long Phoenix MCP waits for approval before returning a pending response. Approvals completed in time return their result in the same call.
tokens.nameDuplicateError: A token with this name (or equivalent slug) already exists.
tokens.nameFormatError: Name must be 3-32 characters: letters, digits, _ or -.
tokens.nameRuleError: 3-32 characters: letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores.
tokens.passThroughModeHelp: Bypass the permission tree for broad entity access. Protected capabilities, MESA rules, the Phoenix MCP blocklist, and sensitive attribute removal still apply.
tokens.postCreateChatSub: Chat from this panel using your own model provider. Opens Settings.
tokens.postCreateConnectSub: Configure an MCP client such as Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, or Gemini.
tokens.postCreateQuestion: How will you use this token?
tokens.postCreateReplaceNote: To use this token, either replace the token in your agent's existing Phoenix MCP server config, or add Phoenix MCP as a new MCP server with this token.
tokens.postCreateShowSub: Reveal the token to copy. It is shown only once.
tokens.presetDeleteBody: The saved snapshot {name} will be permanently removed. The token's current settings are not affected.
tokens.presetEmpty: No presets yet. Save the current settings as this token's first preset.
tokens.presetHint: Changes you make to this token are saved into the active preset when you switch. Applying the active preset reverts to its saved state.
tokens.presetMax: A token can have at most {max} presets.
tokens.presetModifiedTitle: This token's settings have unsaved changes; switching presets saves them into this preset.
tokens.presetNoChange: This preset matches the current settings; only the active label changes.
tokens.presetPtUnderstand: I understand this preset enables pass-through
tokens.presetPtWarning: This preset enables pass-through mode, giving the token broad entity access. Protected capabilities, MESA rules, the Phoenix MCP blocklist, and sensitive attribute removal still apply.
tokens.presetRenameTitle: Rename this preset; saves when you click away
tokens.presetRevertBody: This discards the unsaved changes on {name}:
tokens.presetSwitchSaveInto: Your unsaved changes will first be saved into {name}:
tokens.ptConvertBody: Switching to scoped mode applies the saved permission tree immediately. If it has no grants, this token will lose entity access until you add them.
tokens.ptHeaderBanner: This is a pass-through token. It has broad access to Home Assistant entities and services. Protected capabilities, MESA rules, sensitive attribute removal, and the Phoenix MCP domain block remain active.
tokens.ptNoticeCaps: Pass-through allows reads and everyday actions automatically. Configuration changes, system actions, high-risk capabilities, and system log access still use the Capabilities settings. Confirm always requires approval.
tokens.ptNoticeIntro: Pass-through token. This token bypasses the permission tree and has broad access to Home Assistant entities and services. Sensitive attributes are removed, protected capabilities still apply, and the Phoenix MCP domain remains blocked.
tokens.ptNoticeUsage: Pass-through can send information about every entity to the model, increasing model usage. A scoped permission tree keeps that context smaller.
tokens.rateLimitingDisabled: Rate limiting is disabled for this token.
tokens.rawTokenNote: This token will not be shown again. Copy it now before closing.
tokens.reconnectBanner: Reconnect your agent. This token's available tools have changed.
tokens.revokeBody: Revoking permanently deactivates this token and disconnects every client using it. It cannot be re-enabled.
tokens.revokeCheck: I understand this token will be permanently deactivated
tokens.rotateBody: Rotating immediately invalidates the current value. The new token is shown once. Update every connected client after rotating.
tokens.rotateCheck: I understand the current token value will be invalidated immediately
tokens.rotatedBanner: The old token no longer works. Update this new token in your agent's MCP server config so it keeps working.
tokens.rotatedNote: The old token value is now invalid. Copy the new token before closing; it will not be shown again.
tokens.tokenRenameTitle: Rename this token; saves when you click away

wizard.accessSub: Expand the light group and choose a light you can verify. Select W to grant read and write access. Grant a whole device or expand it to choose one entity. You can add more permissions later.
wizard.agentClaudeHint: Run this in your terminal, then check it with claude mcp list.
wizard.agentCodexIntro: The Codex CLI adds only stdio servers. Use the app settings or edit the configuration file below.
wizard.agentCursorIntro: Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json for all projects, or .cursor/mcp.json for one project. Then enable the server under Cursor Settings > MCP.
wizard.agentOtherIntro: Standard MCP configuration using the streamable-http transport.
wizard.chatReadySub: You can test your agent now using the Agent Chat window. A test question is already typed in for you; press Send. This wizard closes once you send your first prompt.
wizard.choiceAppBody: Use Claude, an IDE, or another MCP-capable app. You copy a connection command that carries your token.
wizard.choiceChatBody: Chat in a window right here in Home Assistant. Bring an API key from a model provider, or a local Ollama server. Nothing to install.
wizard.chooseSub: You can chat with your agent entirely within Home Assistant using the API key or local hostname of your model provider. Optionally, you can use an external app to connect to Phoenix MCP. Select your preferred option:
wizard.codexAppSettingsHint: Open Settings > MCP Servers > Add Server. Use {serverName} as the name, choose Streamable HTTP, and paste the URL above. Leave "Bearer token env var" empty. Add the header values below, then save.
wizard.codexConfigFileHint: Put this block in that file.
wizard.codexEnvHint: On macOS or Linux, run this command and add it to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc. On Windows PowerShell, run: setx {envVar} "<your token>". Do not put the token in config.toml.
wizard.connectAgentTitle: Connect Phoenix MCP to your AI agent
wizard.connectIntro: Add Phoenix MCP as an MCP server in your agent. It authenticates with Authorization: Bearer , not Home Assistant login or OAuth.
wizard.connected: Connected! Your agent reached Phoenix MCP.
wizard.doneSub: Token {name} is ready. You can change its capabilities and permissions from the token page. Revoke it when it is no longer needed, then delete it from Archived tokens.
wizard.mesaHint: MESA may require approval for control actions. The read prompt is enough to verify the connection.
wizard.nameError: Name must be 3-32 characters: letters, digits, _ or -.
wizard.noLights: No lights found in this Home Assistant.
wizard.personaSub: Create a scoped test token, grant access to one device, and connect your agent. New user is selected as a cautious starting point. Choose another persona if needed.
wizard.promptChat: How many lights are in my home?
wizard.providerAddFirst: Add a provider account to continue.
wizard.providerIntro: Agent Chat runs your agent inside Home Assistant using your own model provider account.
wizard.providerPickExisting: Pick an account you already added, or add a new one.
wizard.serverNameHint: Each token uses a separate server name. You can save several in one client, but enable only one phx-* server at a time to avoid duplicate tools with different permissions.
wizard.skillClaudeHint: Install the Phoenix MCP guide as a Claude Code skill. Run this in your terminal.
wizard.skillCodexHint: Download the guide and add or link it in your Codex project instructions. Codex can also fetch it from the URL below.
wizard.skillCursorHint: Save the Phoenix MCP guide as a Cursor project rule. Run this from the project root, then attach it under Cursor Settings > Rules if needed.
wizard.skillGeminiHint: Download the guide and add or link it in GEMINI.md. Gemini can also fetch it from the URL below.
wizard.skillInstallTitle: Optional: install the Phoenix MCP skill
wizard.skillOtherHint: Download the guide and add it to your agent's project context or rules. The agent can also fetch it from the URL below.
wizard.skillSectionBody: Install the Phoenix MCP skill to explain scoped permissions, approvals, and MESA rules to {label}. Phoenix MCP also shares this guidance when the agent connects.
wizard.testSub: Send this prompt to your agent. Phoenix MCP will detect the connection.
wizard.tokenCreatedBanner: Token created. Name and expiry are now fixed; cancel and start over to change them.
wizard.tokenSub: Use a dedicated token for testing. You can change the suggested name now. The name and expiry cannot be changed after creation.
wizard.urlHint: If the agent runs on another machine or network, use a Home Assistant URL it can reach, such as your Nabu Casa or external HTTPS URL.
wizard.waitingForAgent: Waiting for your agent to connect...

mesa.archiveContainsDefaults: Archive contains {summary} profile(s) plus deployment defaults.
mesa.deleteAreaWarn: Every entity in the "{key}" area that inherits from this profile will fall back to the next level (integration, domain, deployment defaults, then the built-in safety baseline).
mesa.deleteDeviceWarn: Every entity owned by the "{key}" device that inherits from this profile will fall back to the next level (area, integration, domain, deployment defaults, then the built-in safety baseline).
mesa.deleteDomainWarn: Every entity in the "{key}" domain that inherits from this profile will fall back to deployment defaults, then the built-in safety baseline. This can change the effective control mode for many entities at once.
mesa.deleteIntegrationWarn: Every entity created by the "{key}" integration that inherits from this profile will fall back to the next level (domain, deployment defaults, then the built-in safety baseline). This can change the effective control mode for many entities at once.
mesa.discardBody: You have unsaved changes to this profile. They will be lost.
mesa.effectiveNoteCreating: This is what MESA applies to this entity now. The fields below are pre-filled to match; change them only to override it.
mesa.effectiveNoteOverridden: A broader profile overrides this entity's setting (most-restrictive layer wins). The effective mode above is what actually applies.
mesa.emptyState: No MESA profiles yet. Add one to define control, automation impact, and privacy rules for agents.

exportBody.one: Download {count} MESA profile and the deployment defaults as a standard MESA JSON archive.
exportBody.other: Download {count} MESA profiles and the deployment defaults as a standard MESA JSON archive.

mesa.exportNote: The file contains your complete agent safety policy and profile notes. Store it securely.
mesa.helpArea: Applies to every entity in this area unless a more specific (device or entity) profile overrides it.
mesa.helpControlMode: How agents may change this entity. Confirm routes writes through admin approval when MESA is enforced; Read-only and Prohibited block writes.
mesa.helpDevice: Applies to every entity this physical device owns, including ones added later by a firmware or integration update, unless a more specific entity profile overrides it.
mesa.helpDomain: Applies to every entity in this domain unless a more specific (integration, area, device, or entity) profile overrides it.
mesa.helpEffectiveResolution: The final value after applying entity, area, domain, deployment, and built-in rules. From shows the source level; Origin shows who created it.
mesa.helpEnforcementMode: Advisory tells agents the control mode but allows writes. Enforced applies this profile even when the global MESA mode is Advisory. Confirm sends writes for approval.
mesa.helpEntity: The Home Assistant entity this profile describes. Start typing a name or id to search.
mesa.helpIntegration: Applies to entities created by this integration unless an area, device, or entity profile overrides it. Imported vendor profiles also appear here.
mesa.helpPrivacyLevel: Sensitivity of the data this entity exposes to agents.
mesa.helpReversibilityCost: How costly it is to undo a change (time, money, or disruption).
mesa.helpReversible: Whether the effect of a change can be undone.
mesa.helpSideEffectScope: How far the physical effect of a change reaches.
mesa.helpTags: Standard MESA capability tags shown to agents. Search the list or use the suggestions for this entity's domain.
mesa.helpTriggersAutomations: Whether changing this entity is likely to fire automations. Drives trigger-validation warnings.
mesa.importIntro: Import profiles from a MESA JSON archive. Invalid profiles are skipped and reported. Valid profiles take effect immediately.
mesa.importInvalid: {count} document(s) failed validation and were not imported:
mesa.importNotArchive: Not a MESA profile export (missing the mesa_export root).
mesa.importNotJson: Could not read the file as JSON.

mesa.vendorTitle: Supplied by the integration (mesa_profile.json). Saving creates your own override.

selectBy.grantNoteLabel: This grants access to entities currently in the selected label. New entities are not included automatically. Grant the domain if future entities should inherit access.
selectBy.label: Label

selectBy.noLabels: No labels are defined on any accessible entity.

settings.addProviderFirst: Add a provider account in Agent Chat first.
settings.agentcliGlobalAria: Show Agent Chat throughout Home Assistant
settings.agentcliGlobalHelp: Keep Agent Chat available across tabs and dashboards. When off, it appears only in the Phoenix MCP panel.
settings.agentcliIntro: Chat with Home Assistant using your own model provider. Agent Chat follows the selected token's permissions, approvals, and MESA rules. Add a provider account, then open Agent Chat from the top right corner.
settings.agentcliRemoveBody: Remove {name}? Agent Chat will no longer be able to use this account until you add it again.
settings.agentcliScrollbackHelp: Lines kept for display and conversation context. Use 0 for no history. Recommended: 100 to 500. Maximum: 5,000.
settings.agentcliStepsHelp: Tool rounds the agent runs before pausing to ask whether to continue. Higher means fewer interruptions on deep tasks. Range: 3 to 100.
settings.aiTaskConfigureFirst: Enable and fully configure the AI Task first.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalBody: Data generation actions that do not specify an entity will use Phoenix MCP AI Task.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalNotReady: Select a token, provider account, and model first. Then return here to make Phoenix MCP the default.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalReplaces: Home Assistant allows only one default, so this replaces the current one: {name}.
settings.aiTaskDefaultModalTitle: Make Phoenix MCP the default AI Task?
settings.aiTaskDefaultOff: Use Phoenix MCP when a Data generation action does not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskDefaultOn: Phoenix MCP handles Data generation actions that do not specify an entity.
settings.aiTaskDisableBody: Phoenix MCP AI Task is the current default for Data generation tasks. Disabling it also clears that default. Home Assistant will use another entity if one is available.
settings.aiTaskDisableTitle: Disable the Phoenix MCP AI Task?
settings.aiTaskEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP AI Task as an entity that automations, scripts, and dashboards can use. Use the setup below (recommended), or go to HA > Settings > Voice assistants
settings.aiTaskIntro: Run Home Assistant AI Task actions through Phoenix MCP's model with token permissions, approvals, MESA rules, and audit logging.
settings.aiTaskModelHelp: The model used for this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this AI Task.
settings.aiTaskSetDefaultFailed: Could not set the default AI Task entity.
settings.aiTaskTokenHelp: Controls which entities and actions this AI Task can access.
settings.aiTaskUnsupported: AI Task requires Home Assistant 2025.7 or later and is unavailable on this version.
settings.assistBoundHelp: Only one token can be bound. In your LLM integration, set Control Home Assistant to Phoenix MCP (scoped). Then select that agent under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off Prefer handling commands locally, and make it preferred.
settings.assistIntro: Give an existing Home Assistant LLM integration access to Phoenix MCP's scoped tools. Choose Phoenix MCP (scoped) when configuring that agent. Use Voice Agent (above) if you want Phoenix MCP to manage the model.
settings.assistUnsupported: This feature is not supported by your Home Assistant version.
settings.dataBody: Permanently delete selected Phoenix MCP data. Core Phoenix MCP data, Agent Chat provider keys, and MESA profiles can be deleted separately.
settings.flushIntervalHelp: How often to save the audit log to disk. Never keeps it in memory only.
settings.infoStorageNote: Phoenix MCP configuration is stored in .storage/phoenix_mcp.json and is included in all HA full backups and partial backups of the .storage directory.
settings.injectHelp: Add MESA profile buttons to Home Assistant's Automations, Scripts, Helpers, People, and integration pages. These buttons may need a Phoenix MCP update after a Home Assistant frontend change. Reload Home Assistant after changing this. Admins only.
settings.killSwitchActiveAria: Kill switch active. All Phoenix MCP endpoints are disabled
settings.killSwitchActiveHelp: All Phoenix MCP client requests are now refused. Re-enabling will re-register all Phoenix MCP routes immediately, without an HA restart.
settings.killSwitchActiveLabel: Kill switch ACTIVE - All Phoenix MCP endpoints are disabled
settings.killSwitchInactiveHelp: When enabled, all Phoenix MCP proxy and MCP endpoints are immediately disabled. The admin panel remains accessible.
settings.languageHelp: Panel language. Auto follows your Home Assistant profile.
settings.logAllowedHelp: Record successful requests in the audit log.
settings.logClientIpHelp: Show source IP addresses. When off, they appear as [redacted].
settings.logDeniedHelp: Record denied and not-found requests in the audit log.
settings.logDisableAllHelp: Stops new audit entries. Sensor counters continue to update.
settings.logEntityIdsHelp: Show entity IDs in the resource field. When off, they appear as [redacted].
settings.logRateLimitedHelp: Record requests blocked by a rate limit.
settings.maxLogEntriesHelp: Maximum entries kept in memory and on disk. Lowering this removes the oldest entries immediately.
settings.mesaEnforcedWarning: Entities without a MESA profile use the built-in safety baseline. Locks and alarm panels are blocked; most other domains require approval. Add profiles or deployment defaults before relying on Enforced mode.
settings.mesaModeHelp: Advisory shows warnings but allows calls. Enforced blocks prohibited and read-only actions, and sends confirmation requests to Approvals.
settings.notifyApprovalHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification for new approval requests. The Approvals count always updates.
settings.notifyRateLimitHelp: Send a Home Assistant notification when a token reaches its rate limit, at most once per token each minute.
settings.notifyRateLimitLabel: Notify when a rate limit is reached
settings.presetsHelp: Save named versions of a token's capabilities, permissions, rate limits, and pass-through setting. Enabling this creates a preset from each token's current settings. Switching presets saves the current changes first.
settings.themeHelp: Light, dark, or follow system preference.
settings.voiceAssistSetupCreated: Phoenix MCP created a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent. Removing it does not disable the voice agent.
settings.voiceAssistSetupNone: Create and configure a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent.
settings.voiceConfigureFirst: Select a token, provider, and model first.
settings.voiceDisableBody: Disabling the voice agent also removes the Home Assistant assistant Phoenix MCP created for it. If it was preferred, Home Assistant will use another assistant.
settings.voiceDisableTitle: Disable the Phoenix MCP voice agent?
settings.voiceEnableHelp: Add Phoenix MCP as a conversation agent. Use the setup below (recommended), or select Phoenix MCP under HA > Settings > Voice assistants, turn off "Prefer handling commands locally," and make it preferred.
settings.voiceIntro: Run a Home Assistant voice assistant through Phoenix MCP's model with token permissions, approvals, MESA rules, and audit logging. No separate LLM integration is needed.
settings.voiceModelHelp: The model used for this voice agent.
settings.voicePreferredHelp: Use Phoenix MCP by default. You can change this under Settings > Voice assistants.
settings.voicePreferredLabel: Make Phoenix MCP my preferred assistant
settings.voiceProviderHelp: The provider account used to run this voice agent.
settings.voiceRemoveBody: This removes the Home Assistant assistant Phoenix MCP created. The Phoenix MCP voice agent remains enabled and can be set up again. If it is preferred, Home Assistant will use another assistant.
settings.voiceRemoveFailed: Could not remove the Phoenix MCP assistant.
settings.voiceSetUpFailed: Could not set up the Phoenix MCP assistant.
settings.voiceSetupBody: Phoenix MCP can create a Home Assistant assistant for this voice agent. You can also configure it under Settings > Voice assistants.
settings.voiceSetupNotReady: Select a token, provider account, and model first, then reopen setup. You can still configure it manually now.
settings.voiceSetupTitle: Set up the Phoenix MCP voice assistant
settings.voiceTokenHelp: Controls which entities and actions this voice agent can access.
settings.wipeCoreHelp: Tokens, permissions, capabilities, settings, configuration history, and audit logs. Active tokens stop working immediately.
settings.wipeMesaHelp: All MESA profiles and dismissed suggestions. This stays off by default to preserve your safety policy.
settings.wipeProvidersHelp: All Agent Chat provider accounts and stored API keys. This is separate from all Phoenix MCP data.
settings.wipeWarning: Choose what to delete. This cannot be undone.

mesaSuggestion.blast_radius.risky.other: This {noun} touches {count} risky entities ({shown}) and has no MESA profile of its own; an agent allowed to trigger it controls those entities indirectly, bypassing their own profiles.
mesaSuggestion.concern.alarm_control_panel: arms and disarms the home security system; a silent disarm defeats it
mesaSuggestion.concern.lock: controls a physical security boundary; a mistaken unlock cannot be undone remotely
mesaSuggestion.concern.siren: sounds a loud alarm; false activation disturbs occupants and neighbours
mesaSuggestion.concern.update: firmware updates are effectively irreversible and can brick the device
mesaSuggestion.concern.valve: controls water or gas flow; a wrong state can flood or vent unattended
mesaSuggestion.concern.water_heater: reaches scald temperatures and burns energy; slow to recover
mesaSuggestion.naked_risky.domain: {count} {domain} entities have no MESA profile at any level. This domain {concern}. A domain-level profile covers them all at once.{baseline_note}
